tickets.title: Decide: test the playground in Firefox and Safari (and in CI), or document Chrome-only as final
tickets.body:
`web/test.sh` (docs/testing.md, "Browser tests") runs the playground tests in headless Chrome only, locally; they are not in `nix flake check` because Chrome isn't in the Nix build sandbox and one test waits out the real 15 s timeout. Firefox and Safari are untested. The goal is a public static site (see the playground notes), so other browsers will be used.

First step: decide (a) a manual cross-browser checklist run before a public release, (b) Firefox via WebDriver BiDi/Playwright in the same script, (c) leave as is. Safari can only be tested on a Mac.

Done when: the decision is recorded in docs/testing.md, plus the script/checklist if (a) or (b).

tickets.title: Records stage 2: projections and eta in the kernel
tickets.body:
Kernel projections and eta, so `p = (p.fst, p.snd)` holds by `rfl` for pairs and records (docs/aoc-2025.md:1302-1303, 'No pair eta'); see docs/proposals/records.md draft 2 §7 (Stage 2: projections and eta in the kernel). Includes the same-type rule and eta off in unification's `first_order` fallback. Do after proof irrelevance (SW-93) is decided.

D8 (Matt, 19 Oct): not now; build when proofs about records need it.

History: this was the 'Records follow-ups' umbrella. Split 19 Oct into SW-119 (done), SW-120 (termination through record fields, backlog), SW-121 (done); (.name) sections done (74db93a). 21 Oct review: `==` for records with proof fields is partly done (derived DecEq handles proofs of equations in DecEq types; other proof fields still E-INSTANCE-NONE, examples/reject/record-eqeq-proof-field.sw) -> SW-202; JS boundary proof fields for ordinary data types -> SW-203.

Done when: `theorem eta (p: Pair a b): p = (p.fst, p.snd) := rfl` checks for pairs and for a record, with the tests of records.md §14.

22 Oct 2026: D503 (Matt: yes) — build record eta after generated ext lemmas and glued values stage 1 land (both touch conversion).

Reminder (D1981, Matt, 30 Oct 2026): once proof irrelevance (SW-93) is built, record eta must apply only to records with at least one field that isn't a proof. A record whose fields are all proofs then behaves like a unit type, and eta on it breaks transitivity of conversion (docs/research/kernel.md §5.2; Lennon-Bertrand FSCD25, Rosain et al. POPL26; Rocq requires at least one relevant field). records.md §7.1 condition 4 should say so.

From SW-568 (merged, backlog review 4 Nov 2026): 'No eta for records in conversion': `p = { row = p.row, column = p.column }` needs a match on p. Sightings: rogue PROOFS.md, SW-960 (4), SW-990 (4), SW-999 (3). The D1981 reminder above is the same text. SW-789 stays as the decision; its 'D8: not now' is overtaken because at least four lanes have now needed eta, so SW-789 is the live question.

tickets.title: WebAssembly stack guard: measure limits in all browsers (incl. compact text) and choose the guard size
tickets.body:
Problem: each call uses stack in linear memory (which the guard measures) and the engine's own call stack (about 1 MiB in V8); the engine's runs out first, so the guard is 256 KiB (crates/web/build.rs, WASM_GUARD; override STITCHWORT_GUARD; it was 128 KiB until games/rogue's 11-field `State` was bundled), calibrated in Node and Chrome only. Firefox and Safari are unmeasured. 256 KiB gives about 25 levels of nesting and list literals of about 200 elements, with a margin of 2 only in Node/Chrome. The parser's stack use per level could also be cut (e.g. boxing `Diagnostic` in its `Result`): that is SW-126.

Change, one campaign: measure in all four engines with web/stress.html: nesting depth, long list/text literals (including compact `List Char` literals, d4d3626, which were only measured natively: the limit before E-RESOURCE and the time), then pick the guard size.

Eliminating recursion (stack-safe-evaluation steps 3 and 4, docs/proposals/stack-safe-evaluation.md) is the real fix; see also SW-62 (long literals) and SW-57 (JS limits in browsers, different subject: generated code).

Done when: a table of limits per browser (nesting, literal length, compact text) is in docs/evaluator-speed.md or compact-text.md and the guard is set from it.

History: split 19 Oct into SW-126; merged SW-61 (guard size) and SW-52 (compact text in WASM).

tickets.title: Proof irrelevance stage 1: proof-position masks in conversion (D1′)
tickets.body:
Implement stage 1 of docs/proposals/proof-irrelevance.md (draft 5, 688de314c; D1′ with D2349, D2352-D2354, D1980). Opus. After SW-1226, before SW-1227 (D2348).

Order (one branch, commits per step, §9):
0. D1980 (§7.11): E-PROP-ELIM refuses a proposition whose constructor field mentions itself. Measure first (std builds, examples/ pass, `stitchwort check` on aoc/ and games/rogue: no E-PROP-ELIM); stop and report if anything relies on it. Test 26.
1. Marks: Def::inert_params (length = arity) and data proof_params, computed in install_group / declare_data on both checked and trusted paths (no check-cache format change); std listing; reference validator; native test (§7.3).
2. conv skips with J and arity boundaries; same_stuck_trees: all-impossible cases equal without comparing scrutinees; reference conv (§7.2).
3. Shortcut mode at K1-K4, CallMemo and TreeMemo keyed by mode, reference R1-R3 and EQUAL_CALLS (§7.2 table).
4. Unifier (§7.5): masks with the whole-metavariable rule via solve; mode at U1-U5.
5. Tests §8: 1-30 + 11b, unit tests, enumerated equivalence/gluing test, three-way runs (17-19, 24, 25, 27), mutations (temporary edits, results recorded here).
6. Docs: docs/core.md (rule, glued calls, precondition, D1981), DESIGN §6, doc comments (§7.4), unify_index.rs:184 comment, mutual-recursion.md §6.7.

Done when: all §8 tests pass and the three-way runs agree; each listed mutation fails its named tests (recorded here); sameMod (§2.1) and handBuilt (§2.2) check by rfl; std inert listing matches §7.3's table or differences are explained here; reference validator passes over std and test programs; bench: nothing >10% slower, anything >5% explained; hash snapshots unchanged or each change explained; merge tier green; daily-tier run (ask Matt first, D2348) green, including the STITCHWORT_GLUE=0 corpus run.

Expected: 480 min (step 0 ~45; marks+analysis ~120; skips+modes ~150; unifier ~60; tests ~90; docs ~15). Checkpoint report after step 0 and after step 3.

(Draft 3's body and the dialExt example were replaced 4 Nov by SW-1268's draft 5; dialExt no longer exists in aoc/.)

WARNING, read before starting (Matt, 30 Oct 2026; from the kernel research register, docs/research/kernel.md §5.1, read in full texts): the recursive-proposition trap. If a proposition can be eliminated into data AND holds a proof of itself in a field, definitional proof irrelevance makes conversion undecidable: any proof X can be unfolded once more, X ≡ MkLoop (Loop.inv X), with no bound on how many unfoldings conversion must try (Gilbert et al. POPL19 §2.3; Abel & Coquand; Lean answered with lean4#13851/#14977). Stitchwort accepts such a type TODAY: E-PROP-ELIM (crates/core/src/check.rs:915-929) lets a single-constructor Prop whose fields are all Prop eliminate into data, without asking whether a field mentions the type itself. Checked by the orchestrator on 30 Oct with main's binary: `type Loop: Prop = | MkLoop (next: Loop)` with `def steps (l: Loop): Nat := match l with | MkLoop n => Succ (steps n)` checks. It is harmless now (no definitional irrelevance yet), but becomes the trap once D1′ masks proof positions. proof-irrelevance.md §5.1 currently defends Loop by making D1′ deliberately incomplete; the register recommends closing the hole instead: add a condition to E-PROP-ELIM that no constructor field mentions the type itself (Lean's rule), after measuring that nothing in std, examples, AoC or rogue relies on it (register ticket T2; decision D1980, open). Do this BEFORE or AS PART OF stage 1, with Loop/steps as a must-reject test.


D1980 (Matt, 30 Oct 2026): yes, refuse eliminating a self-referential proposition into data (the warning above), but as part of THIS ticket's work, not before it: when SW-93 starts, measure first that nothing in std, examples, AoC or rogue eliminates such a proposition into data, then add the E-PROP-ELIM condition with Loop/steps as a must-reject test.
Reminder (D1981, Matt, 30 Oct): record eta interacts with this ticket. Once proofs are irrelevant, a record whose fields are all proofs behaves like a unit type, and eta on it breaks transitivity of conversion (docs/research/kernel.md §5.2; Lennon-Bertrand FSCD25, Rosain et al. POPL26, Rocq requires a relevant field). If record eta (SW-55/SW-789) exists or lands after this, it must be limited to records with at least one field that isn't a proof.


D2348 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): yes, schedule as designed (docs/proposals/proof-irrelevance.md, D1-prime, decided 19 Oct). Opus. After SW-1226 merges, before SW-1227 (both touch the unifier). Merge tier plus a daily-tier run (ask Matt first). Then revisit D2180: if h: equations for any condition.


D2349 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): restrict masks at definitions' arguments to proof parameters the definition never computes on (no case, J or Quot.ind on it, only passed to other masked positions); constructor fields masked as before. Reason: glued calls (SW-257, after draft 3) compare same-head calls argument-first, so unrestricted masks reintroduce Carneiro's non-transitivity (steps l 0 / cast rfl x) and make gluing change what is accepted. D2350: draft 4 of the note first (SW-1250).


Decided by the orchestrator, delegated by Matt (4 Nov 2026: "above my pay grade - can you make good decisions?"), per note draft 4: D2352 yes (shortcut mode: inert arguments skipped, constructor proof fields compared); D2353 yes (an impossible case, as in Void.absurd, is not computing); D2354 yes (storing a proof parameter in a constructor field makes it non-inert); D2355 yes (independent Opus review of the new parts of 5.1, 5.7, 7.1-7.3, 7.10 before stage 1; to start when Matt lifts the hold on new lanes). tickets.title: Array type with get/set/length
tickets.body:
A compact native `Array a` with get/set/length (like compact text), proposed as capability #4 in docs/aoc-2025.md:688 for days 4, 8 and 9. The std library has `Vec` (length-indexed, std/Vec/Vec.sw) but it is a linked list, so access is O(n). Concrete use case (D107, 20 Oct 2026): AoC day 4 part 2 would use a worklist (remove a roll, recheck its 8 neighbours) with O(1) grid access; today `sweep` (aoc/src/Aoc/Day04/Day04.sw:112) walks the whole grid about 60 times (5 s). Large item: design note first (Opus), then a design review before building.

First step: measure whether it is really needed now that days 4 to 7 exist (aoc-2025.md says to measure after days 4-5) and whether `Vec`-based approaches suffice; then the design note (kernel representation, how it hashes, proofs about it, JS extraction as a JS array, and what `set` costs in a pure language: copy vs persistent structure).

Done when: the measurement and note exist and a build/don't-build decision is recorded; building is a separate ticket.

History: D107; aoc-2025.md capability #4.

22 Oct 2026 (day 4 research, D427): day 4 doesn't need a native array — the committed Vec program runs in 0.61 s, a Set worklist in 1.65 s. If an array is built, it should carry its length in the type (bjornestol's Lean day 4 spends ~60 lines of Array.set lemmas keeping rows rectangular). docs/comparisons/aoc-day04-community.md.

24 Oct 2026 (board review): wording update. `sweep` (Day04.sw:112) no longer exists: Day 4 now settles with settleRows over Vec (aoc/src/Aoc/Day04/Day04.sw:99, decreasing, SW-276). Days 4 to 9 all exist, so the "measure first" step can be answered from them.

Backlog review, 4 Nov 2026: the motivating paragraph above is out of date. `sweep` and Aoc/Day04/Day04.sw:112 no longer exist (Day 4 is now under aoc/src/Aoc/Year2024/Day04/; `settle` became `decreasing`, 904029fba, SW-276); the 5 s figure is from before. First step now: re-measure Day 4 part 2 (2024) and 2025 days 4/8/9. SW-808 now lists 'array with constant-time indexing' as a DUPLICATE of this ticket, so this is the survivor. Related motivation: SW-813, SW-814 (interpreter and Map speed).

tickets.title: File-private declarations: `private def` visible only in its own file (helpers)
tickets.body:
Problem: helpers (AoC's twice*/window* lemmas, the prelude's Text.splitCons/splitChars) join their namespace; only their own file should see them (Matt, 20 Oct 2026). There's no `private` today: docs/proposals/multi-file.md:498 ('Visibility of declarations: everything'), :1390 (later list), namespaces.md §8 table.

First step: a short design note (docs/proposals/), with the sketch: `private` before def/theorem/type; the name resolves only in its file; two files of one namespace may each have a private `helper` (the full name gets a file-unique part, as Lean does); bodies stay visible to the checker so a public function using a private helper still unfolds in other files' proofs (hides the name, not the definition; unlike Idris `export`); naming it from another file is E-PRIVATE 'private to file X'. Precedents: Lean private, Agda private blocks, Rust, Scala/TS. Design review gate applies.

Done when: the note is reviewed, then `private` is built with accept/reject examples (including the same private name in two files) and the AoC/prelude helpers are marked.

History: Matt, 20 Oct 2026.

tickets.title: Partial callbacks inside List.map run on native, --js and the reference runner, stack-safe
tickets.body:
The problem: A function marked {Partial} (it might run forever) can only be called from other partial code. `List.map` with a partial callback is not yet supported by the runners (native, `--js`, the reference evaluator), so a partial function cannot be mapped over a list. This is lane 3b of docs/proposals/partial-stage-3.md (section 7.4).

The change: make the three runners execute partial callbacks inside `map`, without growing the stack, and counting ticks exactly as the note specifies. The 4e generator gets partial callbacks through `map`.

What it should do: tick counts and traces agree across the runners; the 1M-element speed figures from the note are met; the `partial.rs` tick tests, `run_js`/`run_reference` on the new example and `effect_runtime` pass. Sonnet. Depends on 3a (library and elaborator part) being merged first.

tickets.title: Make calls to partial functions cheaper in the runners (about 3x slower than ordinary calls today)
tickets.body:
The problem: calls to {Partial} functions are about 3x slower than ordinary ones natively and about 2x in JS; half of the native cost is the request node a partial call builds (D1182, docs/proposals/partial-stage-3.md section 5.4).

The change: runner fast paths plus a cheaper request node for partial calls, in both backends (D1182 A+B, lane 3d of the note, section 7.4).

What it should do: keep the change only if it gives at least 1.5x on `p2-collatz` (or the note's model comparison in `partial.rs`) with identical tick traces (D1219). If the gain is smaller, drop it and record the measurement on this ticket. Sonnet.

tickets.title: Run a partial function's tail self-calls as a loop
tickets.body:
The problem: a partial function that calls itself in tail position still builds a request and a frame per call (D1182 C, lane 3e of docs/proposals/partial-stage-3.md).

The change: compile tail self-calls of partial functions to a direct loop in the runners, after SW-469.

What it should do: at least 1.5x faster on the loop shapes in the note (4e loop shapes, `p2-collatz`) with identical tick counts (D1219); otherwise drop it. Sonnet.

tickets.title: Constructor names: should they live inside their type (Quit vs GaveUp ambiguity), or be resolved by expected type?
tickets.body:
The problem: constructors of different union types share one namespace, so two types cannot both have a constructor `Quit`. The roguelike renamed its `Quit` to `GaveUp` for this reason (D2, NOTES stage 1 #8; unchecked wording).

The change: a design discussion with Matt first. Options: constructors nested in their type (`Outcome.Quit`), or resolving a bare name by the expected type, or leaving as is and documenting the rename trick.

What it should do: Matt picks one; if the answer is not "leave as is", a design note in docs/proposals/ follows. Label it `decision` so it shows up.

tickets.title: Parameter untupling: ((row, chars) => ...) where a function on pairs is expected
tickets.body:
The problem: a lambda written with two parameters is refused where a function on pairs is expected, so `.map ((row, chars) => ...)` needs `.map (((row, chars)) => ...)` (extra brackets). Scala 3 splits the pair automatically ("parameter untupling", https://docs.scala-lang.org/scala3/reference/other-new-features/parameter-untupling.html). Found in the roguelike port (NOTES stage 1 #10).

The change: when a lambda with n>1 parameters is checked against a one-argument function on an n-tuple, treat it as a pattern lambda over the tuple.

What it should do: `[(1, "a")].map ((n, s) => ...)` is accepted and means the same as the bracketed form; arities that don't match still give the usual error. Needs Matt's go-ahead because it is a syntax rule.

Board audit (5 Nov 2026): obsolete: xs.map ((a, b) => a + b) checks today; docs/proposals/lambda-syntax.md calls untupling moot. Closed.

tickets.title: Terminal.simulate: make the frame accumulator visible so proofs can do induction over turns
tickets.body:
The problem: the roguelike proofs (PROOFS.md) cannot induct over the turns of a terminal run because `Terminal.simulate` hides its accumulated frames.

The change: expose the frame accumulator (a loop function with the accumulator as an argument and a lemma relating it to `simulate`), as the roguelike proof needs.

What it should do: a theorem about the whole run can be proved by induction over the turn list.

D1376 (26 Oct): left on backlog by Matt

tickets.title: Effect.bindAssoc's proof uses Quot.sound: can it avoid it?
tickets.body:
The problem: `Effect.bindAssoc` (associativity of bind) is assumed as an axiom in std. Every theorem that uses it shows up in `stitchwort audit` with an axiom, and the roguelike had to restructure its code (draw first, then plan) to avoid needing a proved monad law under handlers (rogue PROOFS.md gap 2).

The change: prove it (probably needs a computation-equality/extensionality principle for Comp), or restrict it to the handler-free case.

What it should do: no axiom left in std for the effect monad laws; `audit` clean on the roguelike generation theorems. Related: SW-570 (symbolic stepping through handlers), SW-660.

Board audit (5 Nov 2026): Effect.bindAssoc is a proved theorem since SW-405; what remains is only its use of Quot.sound.

tickets.title: An unannotated lambda inside an {IO} body makes List.map/fold run at {IO} instead of pure
tickets.body:
The problem: in a `main : {IO} ...` body, a lambda without a type annotation passed to an effect-polymorphic List function (map, foldLeft) is given the {IO} row, not the empty row, so a pure fold in main pays effect dispatch (the interpreter builds effect nodes it does not need).

The change: when the lambda body performs no effects, infer the empty row for the lambda (docs/proposals/effect-polymorphic-list.md covers the design; unchecked whether this is already on its roadmap).

What it should do: a pure inline fold inside main costs the same as outside it; a test in the bench or a step-count example shows no effect dispatch. "For Matt": asks for his go-ahead on the inference rule.

The change: write the design note with a soundness argument and a measured cost model; no code until Matt agrees. Related: SW-593 (effect representation change, D1297 trigger met) and SW-1087 (report on handler fast paths).

POPL26; Rocq requires at least one relevant field). records.md §7.1 condition 4 should say so.

tickets.title: Proofs about effectful code run out of resources stepping through handlers symbolically (E-RESOURCE)
tickets.body:
The problem: when a theorem is about code that runs under a handler (for example the roguelike generator under `seeded`), the checker steps through the handler symbolically and hits E-RESOURCE. The roguelike therefore uses one `next()` per turn and derives every roll from an index hash (the "Dice" workaround, SW-571 text below), so its invariants are proved on the pure `resolve` function only.

The change: find out what the checker needs so effectful code can be proved as written (rogue PROOFS.md "Tried" section lists the attempts). Candidate pieces: Effect.bindAssoc without an axiom (SW-548), a lemma "seeded equals list handler", cheaper symbolic stepping.

What it should do: the generation theorems (generatedReachable, generatedFramed, newGameSound, drawn*) are proved over the free-style {Random} generator, and the roguelike goes back to calling `roll` freely, deleting the index-hashing.

Merged in from SW-564 (backlog review, 4 Nov 2026): prove those generation theorems over the free-style generator; blocked by symbolic handler stepping (E-RESOURCE) and the Effect.bindAssoc axiom (PROOFS.md gaps #2-3). Matt asked to revisit, 26 Oct.
Merged in from SW-571 (backlog review, 4 Nov 2026): per-turn Dice is a provability workaround: `step` calls `next()` once and derives every roll by index hashing (dice.upTo (3*index+1) ..., Dice.upTo = lcg(lcg(seed+index*7919)), Turn.sw/Random.sw) instead of calling `roll` freely. Then `seeded seed (step s c) = resolve dice s c` by rfl (Proofs/Step.sw), so all core invariants are proved about pure `resolve` for every seed. Revert to free `roll` once provable (D1305, Matt 26 Oct). Idea, untested: state invariants for any answers to `roll`, not via `seeded`.

tickets.title: Roguelike per-turn Dice is a provability workaround: step calls next() once and derives every roll by index hashing (dice.upTo (3*index+1) …, Dice.upTo = lcg(lcg(seed+index*7919)), Turn.sw/Random.sw) instead of calling roll freely. Why: then seeded seed (step s c) = resolve dice s c by rfl (Proofs/Step.sw), so all core invariants (walls, HP, occupancy, stepValid, replayValid) are proved about pure resolve for every seed. Free roll would lose them until proofs through a handler stop stepping symbolically into E-RESOURCE (see the handler-stepping ticket; Effect.bindAssoc axiom). Idea (untested): state invariants for any answers to roll rather than via seeded. Revert to free roll once provable (D1305, Matt 26 Oct)

The problem: with vm.overcommit_memory=2, `stitchwort run --native` reserves its full 64 GiB up front on the CLI thread and the OS refuses.

The change: size the reservation before the thread starts. That needs the JIT code and the terminal to be movable across threads (open item from NO6/NO7).

Signature defaults, stage 2: exported functions with defaults take a JS options object
tickets.body:
The problem: functions with default arguments (docs/proposals/signature-defaults.md) are exported to JavaScript with positional parameters, so a JS caller cannot omit defaults or name arguments.

The change: generate an options-object entry point for exported defaults (D1355).

What it should do: from JS, `f({ x: 1 })` works with the declared defaults, positional calls still work, and the generated TypeScript types show the optional fields.

tickets.title: Signature defaults, stage 3: constructor calls use field defaults
tickets.body:
The problem: fields can't have default values at construction: every constructor call must write every field.

The change: constructor calls use the defaults declared on the fields (D1346, docs/proposals/signature-defaults.md stage 3).

What it should do: `T (a := 1)` fills missing fields from their declared defaults, the same rules as functions, and hashes of existing code don't change.

Rename the always-true proposition Unit to something else (Truth/Top) and give the data unit type the name Unit
tickets.body:
The problem: `Unit` is a proposition (type Unit: Prop = | Trivial, core/Logic.sw:12), which misleads readers from Scala/Kotlin where Unit is the data type with one value. The data unit type has no name, only `()` (Builtin.UnitType, core/Effect.sw:94). `True` is taken by Bool's constructor. About 113 uses in std + examples (D1367, to consider).

The change: rename the proposition to `Truth` (proof `Trivial`); alternatives `Top` or the symbol `⊤`. Name the data type `Unit`. Hashes change; that is fine (migration cost does not count).

What it should do: `Unit` means the one-value data type everywhere in docs and std; the proposition has its own name; a sweep of std/examples/aoc compiles and audits clean. Needs Matt's choice of name.

Reminder (D1981, Matt, 30 Oct 2026): once proof irrelevance (SW-93) is built, record eta must apply only to records with at least one field that isn't a proof. A record whose fields are all proofs then behaves like a unit type, and eta on it breaks transitivity of conversion (docs/research/kernel.md §5.2; Lennon-Bertrand FSCD25, Rosain et al. 2 Nov 2026 (SW-1085, D2206): one more data point for declaring the mode. Osprey declares it per operation (a value operation, or `control` with abort/once/many resumptions; a handler can't change it), as Koka does with fun/ctl and Lexa does. A declaration would let the runtime take the in-place path without detection, and would give JS extraction the at-most-once guarantee it needs (DESIGN §16 Q9). `many` adds nothing here (every resumption is multi-shot already). tickets.title: Postponable lambda kept from its in-place try can settle a shared type before an earlier postponed lambda is checked (argument-order dependence)
tickets.body:
From the SW-846 lane: in apply_args_postponing (check.rs), a postponable lambda that succeeds when tried in place is kept, so it can solve a metavariable (with the unfolded type) before an earlier postponed lambda is checked; the result depends on argument order (alias-functions.md §4). Check whether the remaining argument-order cases mostly come from this.

Investigated 29 Oct (night), no change. With def Counts: Type := List Nat, Counts.size, twice (f: b -> Nat) (g: b -> Nat) (z: b):
- A: twice (c => c.size) (c => List.length c) (Counts.of 1) rejected (misleading E-CANNOT-INFER from the first try);
- B: lambdas swapped, rejected (E-UNKNOWN-FIELD, c: List ?2) with no lambda postponed;
- C: both c.size, accepted; E1/E2: moving z first changes the inferred call type Counts vs List Nat.
Cause: whichever comparison solves b first decides its name; a later Counts never restores it (alias-functions.md place 3). SW-859's mechanism is one route into it; the §4/AoC cases are already fixed (SW-846) or not this mechanism.
Rules tried with a temporary switch: R1 (after one postponement, postpone all later postponable lambdas) accepts A, E2 but newly rejects examples/accept/lambda-postponed-alias.sw and a record-literal case; R2 (postpone all) accepts A, B, E2 but rejects lambda-postponed-alias.sw and twice (c => Int.abs c) (c => c) 3.
Options for Matt (lane's D1565/D1566): (a) leave, document with place 3; (b) R1; (c) R2; (d) retry with R1 then R2 only when the whole call fails (untested); and fold into a place-3 design (SW-858) where a later unification can restore the alias name. Lane recs: (d) if wanted before place 3, else (a); yes to folding into place 3. Repro files were in the session scratchpad (o/A.sw-F.sw).

tickets.title: Literature research: lessons (how NOT to run it) and where the partial results are; PAUSED
tickets.body:
PAUSED (Matt, 29 Oct 2026). Literature trawl SW-894 went badly. This ticket records how NOT to run it, and where the partial results are. Restart only on Matt's say-so.

== What went wrong (don't repeat) ==
1. Lanes couldn't read papers and nobody checked first. No PDF tool is installed (pdftotext, mutool, qpdf absent) and WebFetch can't read PDFs. Elaboration, proof automation and kernel registers were written largely from abstracts. Fix that works (tested): `nix shell nixpkgs#poppler-utils -c pdftotext paper.pdf -` (package name has a hyphen; `poppler_utils` is the old name and fails). Test the toolchain on a real paper BEFORE starting a lane.
2. Caveats were buried. Each lane listed "sources not reached / abstract only" at the END of its report; the orchestrator relayed the findings and rankings and dropped the caveat. Rule: every register and every report must START with counts: screened / carded / read in full / not read. Every card says "Full text: read (source)" or "NOT READ"; NOT READ supports no ranking or recommendation.
3. Unverified claims were relayed as fact. Lanes said "the session's web-search budget ran out"; the orchestrator first repeated it, then (after one successful search) wrongly said there was no budget, without checking the docs. The docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference, "Session search limit"): an interactive session has 200 WebSearch calls shared with ALL subagents; at the limit searches silently do nothing; refills ~100/hour (v2.1.290+, CLAUDE_CODE_WEB_SEARCH_REFILLS_PER_HOUR); cap raisable via CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION; /clear resets. Seven parallel research lanes at ~30-40 searches each exhaust it. Plan the search budget; run at most one searching lane; lanes report immediately if searches start doing nothing.
4. Too many lanes at once (up to 4, plus helpers). Stopping a lane does NOT stop the reading helpers it spawned; they kept running and reporting after "stop". After stopping a lane, check ListAgents and stop its children.
5. Decision spam: each lane asked 2-3 decisions; the orchestrator listed them all. Keep to one or two decisions at a time.
6. Personal data: the orchestrator once sent Matt's email address to the Unpaywall API (one request, DOI 10.1145/3434341). Never send personal data to any service. Use Semantic Scholar's API (no email needed) for open-access lookups.
7. Leads can be wrong: the kernel redo's readers found the first kernel register misstated papers (Géran says nothing about Lean's level normaliser; the sort-polymorphism paper doesn't use "quality variables" and mechanises nothing; the definitional-inversion paper isn't about Lean with quotients; MetaCoq found one Coq kernel incompleteness, not a soundness bug). Re-derive claims from full texts, never from a previous register.
8. Access problems that remain: ACM DL returns 403 / HTML to scripts; HAL sometimes returns a bot page (check `file x.pdf`); TU Delft repository refused connections; image-only PDFs/slides can't be read (no OCR). Keep a "for Matt to fetch" table.

== Process to use next time ==
Before starting: test pdftotext on a real paper, check the WebSearch budget headroom, give the lane a reserved D-number range and the reading protocol (counts first, read in full or NOT READ, for-Matt-to-fetch table, no personal data). When it reports: verify its counts and a sample of cards against the files before relaying; lead with how much was read. Log progress as you go. Merge only after reading the diff and running the merge tier.

tickets.title: Consider congruence closure in cases (D2000): first show it would simplify existing proofs
tickets.body:
From the proof-automation research register (docs/research/proof-automation.md §5.1, ticket T1, decision D2000), redone from full texts 30 Oct 2026.

Idea: a congruence-closure step inside `cases`, as in Lean 4's `grind` and every SMT solver, using only the facts already in scope. Equations in scope are grouped into classes of equal terms, closed under "equal arguments give equal results". Two different constructors in one class makes the branch impossible; both sides of the goal in one class proves it. Stage 2 would apply each local ∀ hypothesis once to the matching facts. Probes that fail on main today (register §5.1): (1) `xs = Cons 1 Nil` and `xs = Nil` both in scope; (2) `f a = c` from `a = b` and `f b = c`; (3) `(y: Nat) → lookup = Some y → y < 5` with `lookup = Some y0`, goal `y0 < 5`.

Assumptions of D2000 in full: (A1) comparing class members by their computed form, as `cases` compares atoms now, is enough, without full conversion inside the closure; (A2) the classes at one `cases` node are small (tens of terms), so the step costs little when it fails; (A3) congruence steps written with `J`, with `Bool.uniqueEq` or `DecEq.uniqueEq` equating proof arguments, type-check for the dependent calls the target proofs contain.

D2000 (Matt, 30 Oct 2026): NOT prioritised yet. First gather evidence that it would simplify EXISTING proofs. Before any design: survey std, examples, aoc and games/rogue proofs for steps that chain equations by hand (Eq.trans/Eq.sym/Eq.cong chains, rewrite sequences, matches that only exist to rule out a constructor clash, manual instantiation of a ∀ hypothesis) and that a congruence-closure step in `cases` would make unnecessary; count them, list file:line, and rewrite a few by hand-simulating the step to show the saving. Also cross-check against the cases follow-ups in SW-608. Prioritise only if the survey shows real savings.
30 Oct (survey lane): rebased, read §5.1/D2000, cases.rs closers, proving-guide; starting grep survey of std/examples/aoc/rogue.
30 Oct (survey lane): probes on main: cases fails p2 (even x = True, even x = False ⊢ Void), p3 (o = Some 3, o = None, Option var), p4/p8 injectivity via shared term, p6/p9/p11/p12/p14; passes Nat trans (omega) and h ⊢ h. Writing a leaf classifier for Eq.trans/sym/cong chains next.
30 Oct (survey lane): trial edits (reverted) replacing steps by today's cases: 8 already close (Day06 x5, Day24 settleMore, rogue Loop:24, Rules:24); 12 fail today (Day06 stepTurns, Day16 Moves x3, Day13 Cramer, rogue Loop:20, Day15 sameBox x2, Day17 comboUnique, Day23 x3). Hand-simulating CC on the failures next.
30 Oct (survey lane): 32 sites tried in situ (reverted): 16 already close with today's cases, 16 fail; hand-simulated CC closes 14 of the 16 (3 only with disequality, 1 only with stage 2), 2 unclear. Line savings ~0 per site. Writing docs/research/congruence-closure-evidence.md.

EVIDENCE (30 Oct, branch worktree-agent-a1fb65a24d4a7ede6, 99e85ba2, docs/research/congruence-closure-evidence.md): Congruence closure would close steps today's cases can't, but it saves almost no lines. Candidates (multi-step, all-local leaves; lenient classifier): (a) Eq chains 64 + 11 with And projections; (b) rewrite <locals> in rfl/<local>/at 88/22/19; (c) clash from 2+ local equations 63 (39 are one std Map/Set/Ord shape); (d) local ∀ instantiated 14; (e) helper lemmas 1 (rogue someNotNone, which today's cases already does). 32 sites tried in place (reverted): 16 already close with today's cases, 16 fail. Hand simulation of the 16: 6 close by stage 1 at the root, 4 at the first open case only, 3 only with disequalities, 1 only with stage 2, 2 unclear. Estimate: about 150 sites, about 0 lines each (each step becomes `cases` on the same line, about 30 chars); 4 lines saved in 21 sampled cases; about 10-30 lines across about 70k proof lines. Separately, 389 one-hypothesis clash arms are already closable by today's cases and were never converted. The friction notes have no complaint about chaining local equations; their Eq.trans uses are workarounds through library lemmas, which CC over local facts doesn't reach. Recommendation: DEFER. The evidence that sites exist is moderate (hand simulation, not an implementation). The evidence that line savings are negligible is strong. There is no evidence either way on ease of writing.

D2060 (Matt, 30 Oct 2026): DEFERRED to backlog. Evidence: docs/research/congruence-closure-evidence.md. If revisited, start with the narrower check: two local hypotheses `t = C1` and `t = C2` about the same term with different constructors close the branch (39 of about 75 chain sites), not full congruence closure.

Note (moved from the where field, board audit 5 Nov 2026): deferred (D2060); evidence in docs/research/congruence-closure-evidence.md

tickets.title: Error enumeration for soundness testing (D2031): one type mismatch at every check site, kernel first
tickets.body:
D2031 (infrastructure register C3, §5.1 "Error enumeration", T2), from the Eris paper (Sotiropoulos and Su, PLDI 2026, doi 10.1145/3808320, read in full). Matt, 30 Oct 2026: backlog for now.

Idea: from an accepted program, at every place the checker compares an expression with a known expected type, substitute one expression of an incompatible type (one change per variant); every variant is ill-typed by construction, so any acceptance is a soundness lead. Stage K (kernel, small): over kernel terms, at the check sites in crates/core/src/check.rs (arguments, ascriptions, constructor fields, let values, case branches, definition bodies); oracle: refused with E-TYPE-MISMATCH / E-UNIVERSE / E-REFL; out-of-budget variants dropped. Stage E (elaborator, tooling): source-level, using the hover record of expected types; coercions, postponed comparisons and numeral defaults count as compatible. Options: (a) random overwrites in the existing 400-case daily fuzz run; (b) error enumeration, kernel first, on demand (task fuzz:enum) with a small daily sample. Recommendation: (b), stage K first. Assumptions in full: infrastructure.md §8, D2031.

tickets.title: Memory: resources test reaches 6.7 GB loading one small program repeatedly (sessions not freed?); lsp aoc_navigation test 7.9 GB
tickets.where: lane (D2079): daily tier time + resources memory
tickets.body:
Found while getting the daily tier green (31 Oct 2026). Measured alone with /usr/bin/time -l (peak memory footprint), STITCHWORT_TIER=daily:

- crates/cli/tests/lsp.rs `aoc_navigation_matches_check_index`: 7.9 GB on main, 33 s (9.9 GB, 176 s on 28 Oct, so better than it was). Find whether that's inherent (the whole AoC project in the LSP plus check --index) or held longer than needed.

tickets.title: match last resort: generalise at the end and re-check when only the match's own alternatives fix an unknown (step 4.0 follow-up)
tickets.body:
From SW-817 step 4.0 (D2095, 31 Oct 2026): a generalising match now waits while what it reads holds an unknown. If the only thing that would fix that unknown is the waiting match's own alternatives, it waits for ever and the program is rejected, e.g.
  let g := acc => match List.length [acc] with | Zero => 0 | Succ k => plus acc k
  n   -- g never applied
Main accepted this before step 4.0. Fix as Lean does as a last resort: at the end, generalise anyway, then re-check the choices (occurrence test, motive) once the alternatives have solved the unknown. See postponement.md "As built (step 4.0)". No corpus program has this shape.

tickets.title: Proof hashes differ between debug and release builds (float-playlist example)
tickets.body:
Found 1 Nov 2026 while merging AoC day 10. examples/accept/float-playlist.sw's proofs hash differently in debug and release builds, every run:
- `cargo nextest run --release -p stitchwort-driver --test hash_stability examples` passes (Main.nextStartNotEarlier 460aa8c3…).
- the same without --release fails: nextStartNotEarlier 087ab8f8…, startTimesAscend and playlistAscends also differ. Repeated twice, same values.
So the elaborated proof term depends on the build profile. Hashes are meant to depend only on content.
Untraced suspects: `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` code in elab: queue.rs:1302 `assert_rule_closed` (runs head_meta on waiting items in a debug build only; if that forces or fills a meta, terms can differ) and rows.rs:742; or a float computation that differs in debug.
Impact: merge tier runs --release so it's green; a lane running hash_stability in debug sees a false failure. Correctness: debug assertions must not change what is elaborated.

1 Nov (Opus lane, commit a515d3e1 on worktree-agent-a0344c35ed5b905d8): cause found. Not debug_assertions (skipping assert_rule_closed changed nothing). 41 std declarations hash differently in debug (Std.Nat.partitionPointBounds first; float-playlist inherits it via Float.addMonotoneRight). Cheap attempts that are taken as "no" when they fail (unify::cheaply's let refolding, omega/ring atom comparisons, closing/search match attempts) each had their own 128 KiB / 4 MiB stack budget in bytes; debug frames are bigger, so cheaply failed 790 times in debug vs 7 in release. Fix: Budget::attempt keeps the enclosing operation's stack floor (steps/size/frames limits are the same in every build); an attempt that reaches the floor ends the operation. Regression test: builtins::the_library_hashes_as_in_the_release_build (debug-builtins gate) + 2 budget unit tests. Release hashes unchanged (std, aoc, examples); all examples now match in debug.

tickets.title: BUG: cases panics (value.rs:1011 index underflow) when a proof stops matching the program
tickets.body:
Found by the AoC 2021 day 16 lane (1 Nov 2026), confirmed on main's release binary: `stitchwort check` on the repro below panics at crates/core/src/value.rs:1011:31 "index out of bounds: the len is 1 but the index is 18446744073709551615" (an index underflow, likely a de Bruijn shift). In the repo: flip `if more` to `if not more` in Day16's readGroups, then `stitchwort check Aoc.Year2021.Day16.Proofs`. It happens when a `cases` proof stops matching the program, i.e. exactly when an agent breaks the program on purpose (proving-guide rule 6). Should be an error, never a panic; add the repro to examples/reject once fixed.

Repro (74 lines):
import Std (Bool, DecEq, Eq, List, Nat, Option, Pair, Void)



def readGroups: List Bool → Option (List Nat, List Bool)
  | Cons more (Cons a (Cons b (Cons c (Cons d rest)))) =>
    let group := Nat.fromBits [a, b, c, d]
    if not more then
      match readGroups rest with
        | Some (groups, after) => Some (Cons group groups, after)
        | None => None
    else Some ([group], rest)
  | _ => None

def bitsOf: Nat → Nat → List Bool
  | 0, _ => Nil
  | Succ width, n => bitsOf width (n / 2) ++ [n % 2 == 1]

def groupBits: List Nat → List Bool
  | Nil => Nil
  | Cons group Nil => Cons False (bitsOf 4 group)
  | Cons group rest => Cons True (bitsOf 4 group ++ groupBits rest)

theorem halfOfDouble (acc: Nat) (bit: Bool): (acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit) / 2 = acc :=
  let split := Nat.divModEq (acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit) 2 (omega)
  let below := Nat.modLess (acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit) 2 (omega)
  match bit with
    | True => omega
    | False => omega

theorem parityOfDouble (acc: Nat) (bit: Bool): ((acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit) % 2 == 1) = bit :=
  let split := Nat.divModEq (acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit) 2 (omega)
  let below := Nat.modLess (acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit) 2 (omega)
  match bit with
    | True =>
      let odd: (acc * 2 + 1) % 2 = 1 := omega
      rewrite odd in rfl
    | False =>
      let even: (acc * 2 + 0) % 2 = 0 := omega
      rewrite even in rfl

theorem bitsOfFold (k: Nat): (acc: Nat) → (bits: List Bool) →
    bitsOf (k + bits.length) (List.foldLeft bits acc (acc bit => acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit)) = bitsOf k acc ++ bits
  | acc, Nil => rewrite Nat.addZero k, List.appendNil (bitsOf k acc) in rfl
  | acc, Cons bit rest =>
    let more := bitsOfFold (Succ k) (acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit) rest
    let step: bitsOf (Succ k) (acc * 2 + Bool.toNat bit) ++ rest = bitsOf k acc ++ Cons bit rest :=
      rewrite parityOfDouble acc bit, halfOfDouble acc bit, List.appendAssoc (bitsOf k acc) [bit] rest in rfl
    Eq.trans more step

theorem bitsOfFromBits (bits: List Bool): bitsOf bits.length (Nat.fromBits bits) = bits := bitsOfFold 0 0 bits

theorem fromBitsBelow (bits: List Bool): Nat.fromBits bits < Nat.pow 2 bits.length := omega [Nat.fromBitsFlipped bits]


theorem somePairInjective (x1: a) (y1: b) (x2: a) (y2: b) (h: Some (x1, y1) = Some (x2, y2)): x1 = x2 ∧ y1 = y2 :=
  let both := Option.someInjective _ _ h
  Both (Pair.mkInjectiveFst _ _ _ _ both) (Pair.mkInjectiveSnd _ _ _ _ both)

theorem readGroupsSome: (bits: List Bool) → (groups: List Nat) → (rest: List Bool) → readGroups bits = Some (groups, rest) →
    bits = groupBits groups ++ rest ∧ groups ≠ Nil ∧ groups.all (group => group < 16) = True
  | Cons more (Cons a (Cons b (Cons c (Cons d tail)))), groups, rest, read =>
    let written: bitsOf 4 (Nat.fromBits [a, b, c, d]) = [a, b, c, d] := bitsOfFromBits [a, b, c, d]
    match more with
      | True =>
        match e: readGroups tail with
          | None => cases
          | Some (gs, after) => ?
      | False => ?
  | Nil, groups, rest, read => cases
  | Cons _ Nil, groups, rest, read => cases
  | Cons _ (Cons _ Nil), groups, rest, read => cases
  | Cons _ (Cons _ (Cons _ Nil)), groups, rest, read => cases
  | Cons _ (Cons _ (Cons _ (Cons _ Nil))), groups, rest, read => cases

Progress (Opus lane, 1 Nov): cause found and fixed in 09a54de6 (branch worktree-agent-a492afefe71463e04). cases.rs take_apart evaluated a constructor field's type under the parameters only, but field types are stored under params + earlier fields: Cons's tail `List a` underflowed (the panic); a pair's `snd: b` was read as `a` (wrong-typed fact: a type mismatch, or a fact that missed the goal). Env is now params ++ left side's earlier fields. No other caller shares the pattern. Regression: examples/reject/cases-later-field.sw, examples/accept/cases-later-field.sw. Repro and Day16 flip now give errors, no panic (repro: E-CASES-BUDGET after ~100 s release, cases splitting Nat.divStep internals; a separate perf issue).

tickets.title: Day 16: bitsOf check time doubles per bit; rewrite of x/2 rewrites inside x%2; catch-all arm learns nothing; search --at fails on ✝ names
tickets.body:
From AoC 2021 day 16 (aoc/NOTES-2021.md, 1 Nov 2026). The cases panic is its own ticket (see below in the board).
(1) Checking `bitsOf w n` on an unknown n doubles in time per bit: 8-line repro in NOTES (0.15 s at 9 bits, 0.63 s at 15, 10.1 s at 19). Guess, unverified: nested / 2 and % 2 copy the term. Day 16 proofs take 14 s cold because of it. Workaround: state each step over variables (medium).
(2) rewrite ran out of budget comparing a term with itself (fields vs fields), a side effect of (1). Fix: syntactic comparison first (small).
(3) E-RESOURCE "a value was too large to show … Eq.trans" with no location where a type mismatch belonged: `_` arguments inferred from an already-computed expected type. Same family as SW-963 (2), SW-969 (2), SW-971 (1) (medium).
(4) rewrite of `x / 2` also rewrote inside `x % 2` (which computes to x - x / 2 * 2). Workaround: rewrite % first. Docs line (small).
(5) In `match n with | 0 … | 7 … | _`, the `_` arm learns nothing about n; omega found the model n = 5. Workaround: Succ×8 pattern. Fix: give the catch-all arm the facts n ≠ 0 … n ≠ 7 (small-medium).
(6) Decreasing through an earlier recursive call's result isn't possible; run-time length guards stand in. Docs example (small); results carrying their decrease (large).
(7) Goals list every superseded `read✝` after each match (small).
(8) search --at: refused a goal after a `_` pattern ("E-PARSE: unexpected character `✝`", new, small); refused another "unknown name `group`" (SW-967 (5)); didn't offer a hypothesis as a rewrite (small-medium). ~14 s per query from re-checking the slow namespace.
New evidence SW-960 (3): Bool `a > b` on Nat isn't Nat.decLessThan.
Proof found a real decoder bug (a total-length operator whose length ran past the transmission was accepted; all tests passed).
Std candidates: fixed-width Nat.toBits with round-trip lemmas; takeAppend/dropAppend with a length hypothesis; Some (a, b) injectivity; List.maximum lemmas (imported day 14's maximumSome; SW-971 (7)).

tickets.title: Day 17: omega blind to Int.subNatNatFrom and Bool ||; negative literal fixed as Nat too early (K4); record literal after theorem colon parsed as ability row
tickets.body:
From AoC 2021 day 17 (aoc/NOTES-2021.md, 1 Nov 2026).
(1) [seen twice: also SW-995 item 1, from SW-992] omega fails on `i.toInt + 1 - 1` (both `0 ≤ i.toInt + 1 - 1` and `= i.toInt`): the goal computes to `Int.subNatNatFrom (i + 1) 1 (0 - i)` before omega reads it, an atom it knows nothing about. `0 ≤ i.toInt - 1 + 1` works. 4-line repro in NOTES. Workaround: ring or a lemma over a variable. Fix: read arithmetic as written, or teach omega that call (small-medium).
(2) omega doesn't handle `(p || q) = True` as goal or fact; cases then hit its 64-case budget. Workaround: split into named parts + Bool.orElim/orLeft/orRight. Fix: split such facts, try each side of such goals (small).
(3) New evidence SW-965 (3): search --at missed List.distinctFlatMap because flatMap had computed to List.concat (List.map …).
(4) A negative literal is rejected as Nat too early: in `[(7,2), …, (17,-4)].map (…)`, `-4` gets "a `Nat` can't be negative"; without -4 the numbers become Int. Workaround: annotate List (Int, Int). This is exactly what postponement step 4.3 (K4, number literals wait; branch kept, D2110 pending) addresses; recheck after it lands.
(5) DONE (SW-1015, b0a6af373 / 5b9c4b50e): ~~A record literal right after a theorem's `:` is read as an ability row: E-PARSE "expected `}`, but found `=`", no hint.~~
(6) cases open-case output lists fallback splits like `top = n✝.toInt`, `n✝ ≤ n✝` (small).
Std candidates: Nat.iterateCong (2024 day 22 has a copy too), Nat.iterateKeeps, Int.toNat round-trip lemmas, Int.signCases, 0 ≤ d*(d+1) on Int, 2 * Nat.sumBetween 1 k = k*(k+1).

tickets.title: Day 18: printed goals not valid source (record after constructor, %match names); no per-arm equations; stale variable names in goals; two if forms
tickets.body:
From AoC 2021 day 18 (aoc/NOTES-2021.md, 1 Nov 2026). Termination of snailfish reduction left open (fuel 1000 per sum; completeness up to budget proved).
(1) Printed goals aren't valid source: a record passed to a constructor prints `Cons { value = … } rest` / `Some { found | … }`, which search --at can't read back (E-PARSE: braces after Cons name its fields). Fix: print in brackets (small).
(2) search --at fails on a hidden name: a goal mentioning `split.%match1` gives E-PARSE "expected a field name after '.'" (new effect of SW-971 (3)).
(3) The program had to be reshaped to prove one arm: with a specific `Pair (Regular a) (Regular b)` arm before the general Pair arm, the general arm's equation can't be stated (a written-out match is a different hidden function, E-REFL). Workaround: named helper explodeIn. Fix: generate an equation per arm, like Lean's f.eq_3 (medium).
(4) A goal showed the previous arm's variable names: last arm binds `left1 right1` but goal printed `Pair left right = Pair left2 right2` (printer bug, small-medium).
(5) `if 4 ≤ depth` stays a Bool if (only Nat.leq matching refines it) while `if 10 ≤ value` becomes Decidable.elim (Nat.decLessThan 9 value). Cause guessed. Fix: one form or a proving-guide line (small).
(6) audit can't satisfy `f x = Some y` with y free; fix: compute y from f x rather than random (small-medium; different from SW-967 (8)).
(7) Small: `import Std (Pair)` hides a local Pair constructor (clear message); braces after a constructor bit three times (LSP quick fix); no multi-line string literals (example is Text.join of a list); a recursive {Parse} function needs an explicit bound.
Seen again: no record eta (SW-960 (4)); holes before expected type (SW-969 (2)); context order breaks search --at (SW-969 (1)); search misses DecEq.soundFalse / Nat.equalFalse for == facts (SW-960 (3)); day 14's maximumSome imported again (SW-971 (7)).
Std candidates: xs ≠ Nil → xs ++ ys ≠ Nil (both sides); findIndexFrom = None → p false on every element; List.maximum lemmas.

Board audit (5 Nov 2026): the goals-printing-%match1 item is SW-1004's; dropped here.

tickets.title: BUG: lambda argument becomes unknown x in a termination goal inside a callback (from SW-967 item 2)
tickets.body:
Split from SW-967 item 2 (AoC 2021 day 12). Repro in aoc/NOTES-2021.md day 12: def g (xs: List Nat) (k: Nat): Nat decreasing xs.length := [1, 2] |> .sumBy (other => if k == 0 then 0 else g (xs.filter (c => c == other)) k [decreasing := ?]) shows ⊢ List.length x < List.length xs.

2026-11-01 Opus: cause: sumBy's callback is checked as a computation in an unknown row {e}; the argument xs.filter (…) may perform (filter is effect-polymorphic), so effects::run_first bound it with bind into a hidden variable %4 (trace: the call was rec %4 k, cx names [xs, k, %rec, other, %4]). Same for a let (sequence) and if h: on such a condition (E-ABILITY).
2026-11-01 Opus: fix 517d8d1e: such an expression is first elaborated as plain calls (check::pure_first); if pure it's a transparent let (args, lets) or a pure if. Goal now shows List.length (List.filter xs (c => c == other)) < List.length xs. Tests: examples/goals + examples/accept decreasing-callback-argument. Hashes: 975 of 13877 std+aoc decls change (mostly AoC tests/mains/parsers in Fail/Parse/IO rows: bind of a pure call became a let).

tickets.title: BUG: match on a bounded search computes the scrutinee (E-RESOURCE) (from SW-965 item 1)
tickets.body:
Split from SW-965 item 1 (AoC 2021 day 11). Repro in aoc/NOTES-2021.md day 11 (13 lines): match on search xs 1 10000 fails E-RESOURCE 'a value was too large to show'; 100 steps 0.11 s, 1000 0.68 s.

Progress (Opus, 1 Nov): cause: matching.rs `lifted` read every expression scrutinee back in full for the occurrence test (backtrace check_match -> quote -> quote_as at the size limit); the unfolded search is quadratic in the bound. Fix 4a3c6c77 on worktree-agent-a11b6d4a28891900d: a single scrutinee is read back capped at the size of the largest term it could occur in (goal, variable types, its own type); larger means it occurs nowhere. Open: a goal that really mentions the huge scrutinee still runs out (now labelled at the match).

tickets.title: search on real goals (D2116): AoC benchmark, then stop --at refusals, then better candidates
tickets.body:
From AoC 2021 days 9-18 (1 Nov 2026). (1) Benchmark: the ~40 goals AoC lanes recorded with what closed them (NOTES-2021 day sections, friction tickets SW-960..980) plus the query log; record search --at's hit rate on main first. tickets.title: Kernel: refine context types lazily at case splits (case cost O(cases x context) today; lifts SW-1053's 64-hypothesis cap); also count Int/char literal hypotheses toward the cap
tickets.body:
From SW-1053 (2 Nov 2026). The kernel refines the whole context at every case: check_num_case (crates/core/src/check.rs:1195 on 4 Nov, its `refined` closure at :1249-1254) runs substitute_in over the whole environment and every context type — a read-back and re-evaluation per entry — at each number; check_case (begins at :853) does the same per constructor. So a case split with many hypotheses in scope costs O(cases x context). This is why a catch-all equation after N number arms costs N^2 (SW-1053 capped it at 64).

Idea: record the pending substitution per branch (variable, value, environment) and apply it to an entry's type only when it is looked up (variable type lookup ~line 243; the matched variable's type ~870, ~1215; nested case refinement and the index unifier apply what's pending first). Entries that are just their own variable can be skipped outright (cheap and safe on its own). Effect: each arm of an equation proof touches only its hypothesis and the goal, so the cap could be lifted.

Cost/risk: trusted kernel. Must stay equivalent to eager refinement (eval(quote_folded(v)) gives the same value), keep checked terms and hashes (Term::Eq's filled-in type is read back from these types), and compose nested refinements in order. Skipping entries that don't mention the variable doesn't help here (every hypothesis mentions it).

Also from SW-1053: the 64 cap counts only Nat hypotheses — Int literal hypotheses aren't counted, and a big character table's merged notListed is one hypothesis with the same N^2 proof cost. Cover those with the cap (small) unless this kernel change lands first.

Backlog review, 4 Nov 2026: SW-1106 (done, 20f98102d 'a branch's refinement returns values that don't mention the matched variable as they are') already removed part of the cost. What remains: the per-entry read-back and re-evaluation for entries whose type does mention the variable; re-measure before building.

Known failing daily-tier test at push (2 Nov 2026): stitchwort-driver::function_equations a_match_below_a_lifted_alternative_refines_where_its_variable_is_bound — `deeper.eq2.some.nil` isn't generated (function_equations.rs:109). SW-1069's nested-match case (def deeper: `Cons x rest => match List.head rest with | Some y => match rest with | Nil => x | Cons z more => y + z | None => 1`).

It passed when SW-1069/1071 merged (lane ran it), so SW-1077 (closed-condition skip, CLOSED_SPLIT in crates/elab/src/equations.rs) or de25c46e (the if h: condition fix to that skip) probably broke it. Tried and reverted (didn't fix it): exempting a constructor-headed scrutinee from the match-side closed check (equations.rs ~2965). Cause unknown. A missing equation, not unsoundness.

Next: bisect SW-1077's merge vs de25c46e with only this test plus branch_equations, an_overlapped_arms_branches_are_read_from_each_case, the_walls_errors_name_the_branch_equations; fix; rerun only those (Matt: strict test budget).


Cause (found 2 Nov 2026, Speedwell, by reading the code; no bisect run needed): SW-1077's match-side CLOSED_SPLIT check (bf554bea). de25c46e only touched the if-side check, and deeper has no if. For eq2.some.nil the first run asks to refine rest (bound in the row) to Nil; in the refined run the outer scrutinee List.head rest becomes List.head Nil, which is closed, so the branch was skipped. The test expects exactly that closed hypothesis (isSome: List.head [] = Some y). The earlier constructor-head exemption missed it because List.head Nil is headed by a Def.

Fix (uncommitted in the working tree): both CLOSED_SPLIT checks in branch_run (if and match) apply only when refines is empty, i.e. on the unrefined run, which meets any term that is closed in the program first. Trade-off: a split that is closed in the program and lies below the step where the first run stopped to ask for a refinement is now stated, not skipped. That costs kernel work but is sound, and the case is narrow.

Tests run: function_equations, the 4 targeted tests (a_match_below..., branch_equations, an_overlapped_arms..., the_walls_errors...): 4/4 ok. rustfmt clean. Hashes lane tier (STITCHWORT_TIER=lane, profile lane-hashes: hash_stability examples/projects/prelude + pinned_hashes): 5/5 passed, so no snapshot changes. Ready to commit.

tickets.body:
Analysis (read-only Explore agent, 2 Nov 2026; code read, nothing run; medium confidence on the mechanism):
- Loading isn't the difference: search --at loads all std up front for every goal (load_all_libraries, crates/cli/src/main.rs:1857; driver search_at.rs:1567, :1670). Goals 1/3 0.29 GB vs goal 2 1.5 GB comes from searching and checking.
- closing_plans turns the constants filter off (filter: false, crates/elab/src/closing.rs:365), so every declaration is unified with the goal. ≤ on Nat is the built-in Nat.LessEq, which unfolds to `… = True`, so any `_ = True` conclusion matches, including generated equations from unrelated files (closing.rs:421-424 cites Char.isAsciiSpaceCode.eq1 closing a Float.ieeeLe goal). Each match gets several plans (hypotheses h1, h2) and each is tried with rfl/omega/cases/byDecision (search_at.rs:1250); search.md:1165 records one cases check at 1.2 GB.
- Memory held: Globals defs/datas (core/src/globals.rs:421), whole-library generated equations (search_at.rs:612), lifted <input N> definitions kept per check (lib.rs:1178); nothing freed until main.rs:1888.
- Levers: filter on in closing_plans (or overlaps, search.rs:893) with the relaxed second pass as fallback; skip generated equations sharing no data type with the goal; load only the goal's needs (library.rs:1002 load_needs); per-check memory/step caps or no cases on obligations (today time only, search_at.rs:541).
Plan when picked up (Opus): confirm with STITCHWORT_SEARCH_DEBUG per-check timings; then the filter with fallback; report memory and the AoC closing rate (66% today, SW-915) before/after. tickets.title: Research: Osprey's effects (https://www.ospreylang.dev/docs/effects/) - what it is, and what Stitchwort's abilities/handlers could borrow
tickets.body:
Result (Opus research lane, 2 Nov 2026; read-only). Osprey: functional language in Rust -> LLVM by one author (Nimblesite), repo since June 2025, v0.28, ~65 stars, spec well ahead of what's built; a credible prototype, not a reference design. Effects: per-operation modes (value vs control abort/once/many), deep handlers, handler values or block-scoped `handle`, rows by inclusion (open rows a prototype), `handle static` (compile-time discharge or error), Arith effect, replayable, finally/mask/instance (mostly planned).
Stitchwort already same or better: direct style, deep handlers, return clause, unhandled = compile error, row polymorphism built (effect-polymorphism.md 0-3), multi-shot on every runner (D1162), kernel-checked handler termination via Effect.Comp/foldComp (DESIGN §8), handler-based testing plus proofs; Arith not needed (unbounded numbers, / needs a proof).
Candidates, ranked: (1) a "handle static"-style assertion that a handler takes the fused/in-place fast path or says which clause stopped it (fusion.rs reasons; would have caught SW-861): worth doing, as evidence for research T5 (docs/research/effects.md §6). (2) declared operation modes (Koka fun/ctl, Osprey abort/once): maybe, add to SW-791/D1428's options; also answers DESIGN §16 Q9 for JS extraction. (3) differential tests of handler semantics against Koka (nixpkgs koka 3.2.9; port examples/accept/abilities.sw and row tests): worth a low-priority ticket, it checks the trusted translation independently. (4) requirement provenance in diagnostics/hover (Store@3:15.get): maybe, fold into research rank 6. No: mask/named instances (abilities.md:229), finally/replayable, block-scoped handle / second syntax.
Sources: ospreylang.dev/docs/effects/, /spec/0017-algebraiceffects/, /status/, github.com/Nimblesite/osprey (examples/handlers, docs/plans/0016-algebraic-effects-and-handlers.md).

tickets.title: Research: mold linker (https://github.com/rui314/mold) as a quick win for Stitchwort's Rust builds on this Mac and Linux: does it support macOS, how much of our build/test time is linking, what would wiring it in cost
tickets.body: Result (Sonnet research lane, 2 Nov 2026): not worth wiring in. mold is ELF-only now (Mach-O support removed; the macOS port continues commercially as sold); nixpkgs mold 3.0.0 evaluates on aarch64-darwin but can't link Mach-O. Measured here (release, no kache): linking is ~0.4-0.5 s of a 15 s incremental rebuild (touch crates/cli: ~3%), 0.43 s of a 113 s test-binary rebuild (<0.4%); a clean build makes 44 links of ~0.3 s each in parallel. ld-prime and ld64.lld no different (noise, ±0.1-0.2 s). Note: the devShell's linker is nix's ld64-956.6, not Apple's ld-prime. Linux: mold would save at most tenths of a second per 16-22 MB binary; not worth it (musl static path, reproducibility). If Linux links ever take seconds: [target.'cfg(target_os = "linux")'] link-arg=-fuse-ld=mold in .cargo/config.toml plus pkgs.mold/clang in the Linux devShell; measure with --timings first. Build time is rustc/LLVM codegen.

tickets.body:
Step 1 result (Sonnet, 2 Nov 2026; under load 7-37, re-time before citing). SW-861's natural form is fused on the machine now (01462c09): Std.Parse Parse.next over 160,000 chars, natural vs pair form same user time (~4.6-4.8 s vs 4.55-4.64 s), natural 13% less memory (1.39 vs 1.60 GB); the 28 Oct 9.4 s / 2.2 s doesn't reproduce. Discriminator: at 1M operations a fused natural handler completes, an all-non-tail control hits the recursion limit (machine and --js). JS: fuse gets bodies=None so it can't follow a lifted %match; no slowdown seen in --js runs but not confirmed whether those ran on node. Memory grows ~5.8 KB per char in every form (fusion doesn't bound it). SW-738 revert: plausible after a JS check (build --js, big parse in node) and re-running the Parse.runFrom* rfl lemmas. Decline points in fusion.rs (11, each a silent Ok(None) or fallthrough today): partial foldComp; carrier not at the empty row / not state-passing; return clause not Done e; unrecognised handler structure; clause not x,k => ...; k used non-tail at <span>; depth > 200; > 64 matches followed; backend can't see inside match (JS); no arm of a match resumes; no clause resumes. Plus "partly fused" when one clause falls back. Plan: fuse returns Result<Result<Fused, Decline>> with a span; call sites ignore it; `stitchwort check --explain-handlers` calls fuse with the machine's bodies and with None, one line per handler (machine / js / not fused). Phase 1 (Opus, 2 Nov 2026; analysis only, nothing built). Correction: elab is 99k lines of .rs (plus 28k of embedded std .sw), not 188k. The cost of an edit is mostly fan-out: ~165 test binaries, ~135 depend on elab; lanes build all of them because test:one/test:lane run `nextest --workspace` (nextest builds every binary before filtering). A std .sw edit rebuilds the whole stack (include_str! plus driver/build.rs's fingerprint). Dev-dependency-only features (core reference/stack-check, syntax stack-check, rt alloc-trace) likely make `task build` and test builds compile the stack twice (inferred). elab also compiles twice per edit (lib and lib-test, 124 unit tests). Inside elab: 58 of 77 modules (89k lines) are one strongly connected cluster around `impl Elaborator`; no cheap split. Not significant: proc macros (none), generics, build scripts, linking. Release is needed for stack depth (debug ~10x larger frames) and sweep speed.
Ranked: (1) lanes build only the targets they run (--workspace --test X / --lib); (2) one feature set for all builds; (3) std read from disk in dev/test, embedded only in distributed builds (design note); (4) tuned test profile: release + incremental + more codegen units, maybe lower opt-level for elab/tests (measure; stack and kache risks); (5) one test binary per test package (design note); (6) elab's unit tests out of the lib; (7) split elab only if still on the critical path after 1-6. Not on stable: Cranelift, parallel front end.
End state: incremental tuned test profile, one binary per test package, lanes build what they run, one feature set, std from disk except in distributed builds, elab split only if measured necessary. Order 1, 2, 4, 3, 6, 5, then 7.
Measurement plan M0-M8 (~50-60 min machine time on a quiet machine, scratch checkout, kache off, nothing committed); M5's merge-tier comparison needs Matt's approval. Script: scratchpad modgraph.py.

tickets.title: Memory grows ~5.8 KB per input character in Std.Parse loops, fused or not (D2215 b, from SW-1087; noted on SW-861): Parse.next over 160,000 chars peaks 1.2-1.6 GB against 94 MB for the input list; a fused Nat-state handler at 1M operations peaks 6.3 GB. Find what is retained per operation (trail, continuation, sharing, allocator) and fix it. Sonnet; measure on a quiet machine
tickets.body:
Diagnosis (Sonnet, 2 Nov 23:40; no fix, no commit). Not the runtime: the checker. A `match` in `main` on a long effectful call (`match C.run (...) 0 with ...`) is fully evaluated at check time by `matching::generalised_now` -> `normals` (crates/elab/src/matching.rs) with core::value::run (no fusion, no tail resumption), ~7.3-7.8 KB per op, to test whether the scrutinee occurs in the goal. `check cn1m.sw` alone: 7.36 GB, 17 s. Moving the match into a helper (`show (C.run ...)`): cn1m 7.36 GB/18 s -> 69.5 MB/1.0 s; next (160k chars) 1.39 GB/4.6 s -> 101.8 MB/0.43 s; machine slope ~0.06 KB/char (the input list). Machine is bounded (frames=1). Not the allocator, not a leak (alloc-trace).
Consequence: SW-861 and SW-738's natural-vs-workaround memory comparisons measured the checker, not the fused machine; --js pays it too.
Proposed fix (needs Opus + Matt): in `normals`, return None (as the existing size cap does) when the scrutinee can't occur: closed, of an inductive Data type, and no constructor of it in the goal, hypothesis types or other scrutinees' types; or a work budget. Plus a regression test on check's peak memory. Longer term: fusion/tail resumption in core::value. Workaround: pass the handled result through a helper. Scratch helper-form programs: scratchpad/sw-1096/.
Model result: Sonnet, worked (diagnosis), 10 min (est. 45).

Regression rows in crates/bench/tests/check_work.rs (evaluation steps constant in cost). Literature note docs/proposals/match-generalisation-evaluation.md: Lean 4 kabstract never evaluates the discriminant; Agda/Idris normalise like Stitchwort; recommends not moving to Lean's way now (a language decision for Matt). Opus review running.

The API answered a test prompt in 5 s; the same command in the same clone ran fine twice after. Suspects (unconfirmed): two servers starting at once (SW-1092's run was alive at the first hang), the long-lived 'opencode serve --service' sharing opencode.db, 2.1.4 (earlier runs were 2.1.1). tickets.body:
Hang 3, 23:17:46 (run a225c46a, SW-1102 in a new scratch clone scratch-sw-1102): same signature, server 92c3af4c logged 'cli starting' and nothing in 2 min. No other opencode run alive; 'opencode serve --service' (pid 48942, since ~17:36, ppid 1) was. Per D2217 the investigation is brought forward (started 23:21, Sonnet).


Result (Sonnet, 2 Nov 23:41): cause found. With stdin not a terminal, opencode run waits for stdin EOF even with the prompt as an argument; an open pipe that never closes hangs it exactly as seen (server 'cli starting' then nothing). Repro: open pipe 2/2 hang; </dev/null 16/16 fine (reruns, fresh clones, production flags). Upstream anomalyco/opencode#59287 (open; triage says still on dev); 2.2.5 (nixpkgs-unstable) likely still hangs (fake-model test). Project.resolve stack was the idle server's startup fiber being cancelled. Not the serve --service process, not concurrency, not 2.1.4 (the wait is in v1 too, #38723). opencode comes from home.packages in ~/.config/nix-darwin/home/matt.nix:28. Workaround applied: </dev/null in CLAUDE.md and docs/workflow.md. Close after a few real runs start cleanly with it.

tickets.title: Checking a match re-evaluates every context value per branch (core::check::substitute_in), ~1.9 KB per input char
tickets.body:
Found in SW-1096 (3 Nov): after the scrutinee fix, next.sw (Parse.next over 160,000 chars, the input bound by let input) still costs 395 MB at check time, ~1.9 KB per char. A sampled profile shows it in the match's case split: for every branch, core::check::substitute_in reads back and re-evaluates every value in the context, including the 160,000-element list. Core/kernel code: Opus lane, with a design note if the change is more than local.

D2264 (Matt, 3 Nov): start now.

Done 20f98102 (Opus, 75 min, est. 60), reviewed by the orchestrator (Opus), merged. The cost was in the elaborator case splits calling core substitute_in, not the kernel itself. New Unchanged checker (check.rs): a context value is kept as it is when x does not occur in it, every variable carries the Apart facts the identity environment would give, and it has none of: metas, folded defs, quot forms, glued calls with gluing off, closures, NatAdd, Nat Zero/Succ ctors, resumptions, erased fields; else the old path. Soundness needs only the first condition; the rest keep values identical (hashes and terms unchanged; checked by a temporary old-vs-new comparison on every example and std). Shared sequences visited once, keyed by address (all borrowed and immutable for the call). Reproducer (Parse.next on 160k chars): 6.67M -> 0.17M steps, 391-399 MB -> 93 MB. Display difference: inside a branch, a hypothesis holding a glued call that steps at once shows as the call rather than its whole result (as outside the branch); orchestrator call, kept (it is the saving; terms and hashes unchanged). Tests: core 356 (incl. fuzz daily sample), hash_stability 7, cli examples 9; orchestrator reran core + prelude hash, 357.

tickets.title: Parallel checking (deprioritised, D2299): measured ceiling 5.9x cold on aoc, ~3.4x with processes at 1.6-2.7x CPU, no gain for a typical edit
tickets.body:
Parallel checking: deprioritised (D2299, Matt, 4 Nov 2026). Measured in SW-1170; full write-up and scripts in dev/measurements/parallel-checking.md and dev/parallel-check/.

Findings (aoc unless noted; work from measured CPU, wall times under load 30+):
- Cold full check: 67.4 s of work, 11.5 s critical path, so the ceiling is 5.9x (reached at 8 cores). The critical path is two Proofs namespaces of ~8 s; one is mostly a single 6.4 s declaration group. Beyond ~6x needs parallelism inside a namespace.
- One process per namespace (model): ~3.4x (67 s -> 20 s); per day group ~4.0x (17 s). Costs 1.6-2.7x the CPU: each process spends 0.3-0.45 s re-elaborating the core, parsing the project and replaying a median of 30 library files from the cache (112 s CPU over 266 jobs).
- Prototype, 8 processes, library cached: CPU 156-160 s vs 153 s predicted; wall 29.7 s vs 73-108 s sequential (loaded machine, no quiet run).
- Typical edit: no gain (one Proofs/Tests namespace re-checked); a day's code namespace 0.56x (slower); Aoc.Common (59 namespaces) ~1.7x.
- Memory: a worker 130-190 MB after replay, heavy namespaces 0.8-1.3 GB (Day06.Proofs 1.25 GB); 8 workers summed 4.1 GB vs 1.6 GB sequential.
- games/rogue: ceiling 1.76x, processes at most 1.15x. Standard library alone: ceiling 2.2x (deep file chain).
- In-process threads on a frozen shared base (reasoning only): near 5.9x at sequential CPU, but need Rc -> Arc for core terms and Send elaborator state; same critical-path ceiling.

Why deprioritised: cold checks mostly happen in lanes and test tiers on an already saturated machine, where 2.5x the CPU mostly takes cores from other work, and the edit loop doesn't gain.

If revisited: cheapest first step is `check --jobs N` in the driver, one child process per day group along the import graph after the library is checked once, sharing the check cache; est. ~4x cold on a quiet machine, a day or two, no elaborator changes. The Globals split (D2290) keeps the in-process route open.

Related, better value for the edit loop: SW-1193 (warm check replays untouched namespaces, 3.8 s vs 0.5-1.7 s), SW-1194 (0.3 s CPU per process start), SW-1195 (six Proofs namespaces are 59% of a cold check).

Closed 4 Nov 2026 (backlog review): the measurement is the deliverable (merged 10d98d97d; dev/measurements/parallel-checking.md). Matt deprioritised it (D2299). Follow-ups: SW-1193 (done), SW-1194, SW-1195; the `check --jobs N` idea is noted on SW-1194.

tickets.title: fuzz_elab: kernel rejects an elaborated term from a mutated match.sw (full tier)
tickets.body:
Full tier at 1cef1def (SW-1175): fuzz_elab mutated_examples_check_without_internal_errors failed. Oracle 3 (kernel rejected an elaborated term): case 1050, seed 0x5eede1ab00000685, rng state 0xe3a9eaefcf2cbaaa, from accept/match.sw: E-TYPE-MISMATCH. Input saved (copy outside target/) in the orchestrator's scratchpad as 5eede1ab00000685-1050.sw. Find whether this is new tonight (elaborator-state steps 6a-7, SW-1179) or older, minimise, and fix the elaborator so it reports an error or builds a well-typed term. Expected: 60 min.

Progress (Opus, 04:59-05:20): commit 6b93dea2 on lane/SW-1182. Cause: equation generation, not the elaborator proper. `lenZero` in accept/match.sw (`match h: xs.length with | Zero => Yes rfl`) lifts to a helper whose result type mentions the matched column, so branch equations `lenZero.eq.zero/.succ` were stated ill-typed; the kernel refused them (E-REFL, E-TYPE-MISMATCH) and one_equation swallowed that as a skip ("the kernel refused the generated proof"). It happens on the unmutated example too; oracle 3 fired because it matches by message and the mutation added user E-TYPE-MISMATCH errors with the same "type mismatch" message. Not tonight's work: 8cffe0be (before SW-1152) refuses the same two terms. Fix: helper_call skips a match whose helper's result type mentions what it matches, with a reason. Test: function_equations a_generalising_matchs_branches_are_skipped_not_refused. Ran: function_equations + function_induct binaries (14 pass); fuzz_elab with FUZZ_CASES=1051 once (pass, 84 s). Follow-up: oracle 3 matches by message alone, so any swallowed kernel refusal plus an unrelated user error with the same message fails it.


Cause: lenZero in examples/accept/match.sw (a match h: whose helper result type mentions the scrutinee) had ill-typed branch equations the kernel refused silently; the mutation added a user E-TYPE-MISMATCH with the same message, which oracle 3 matched. Pre-existing (reproduced at 8cffe0be). Fix: skip such equations with a reason.
Model result: Opus, worked, 21 min (est. 60)

Cause: Cache::put built the key before checking which cache it was, so even Cache::disabled() formatted a key per test. Fix (bb7d65fb): only the memory cache builds the key. tickets.title: Audit vacuity check: false warnings on generated equations; is random search viable?
tickets.body:
From AoC 2020 day 4 (SW-1249, NOTES-2020.md item 6, ranked 2). The audit's vacuity check tries random inputs and warns when none satisfy a theorem's hypotheses. On day 4 all 8-11 warnings were false, all on compiler-generated equations (heightValid.eq.some with hypothesis value.stripSuffix "cm" = Some number; Spec.validValue.eq.if… with (key == "byr") = True): random texts never hit the literals. Same blindness: check --counterexamples missed a deliberately broken height range (between 151 193). Options raised: (A) skip generated equations in the vacuity check (they come from the definition, so can't be misstated); (B) seed generators with the definition's literals.

D2357 (Matt, 4 Nov): backlog only. Matt doubts random generation is a viable strategy for vacuity at all (hoping it finds inputs); revisit the approach itself (e.g. what a warning should require, or a non-random method) before doing A or B.

From SW-1210 (merged, backlog review 4 Nov 2026), option C: satisfy hypotheses of the form `f x = y` / `f x = Some y` in the counterexample search by computing y from the generated x, so audit tests 'if the program returns X' theorems instead of warning they may be vacuous. From aoc/NOTES-2020.md day 1 item 5: 6 of day 1's 16 theorems gave up this way. Medium, a day or two.
D2306 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): backlog, consider later with evidence from other AoC days (2021/2024/2025 audits will have the same warnings).
Related, kept separate: SW-1063 (custom generators), SW-1247 (generator for non-equation proof fields).

tickets.title: Parse.exactly n parser for exactly n repetitions; named arguments on Parse.repeat ranges
tickets.body:
D2367 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): yes. Every non-std use of Parse.repeat is 'exactly n' (repeat 7 7, repeat 3 3 in 2020 day 5; repeat 10 10, repeat 4 4 in 2021 day 8), which reads oddly. Add Parse.exactly n parser (defined as repeat n n) with Parse.readsExactly, use it wherever repeat has equal bounds (programs and proofs). Remaining range calls name their bounds: Parse.repeat (atLeast := 1) (atMost := 3) p.
