tickets.title: Design note: Scala-style partial-function lambdas (collect) in Stitchwort
tickets.body:
D2368 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): a match whose result is Option does NOT silently default missing cases to None; keep the exhaustiveness check, be explicit. But Matt wants Scala's partial-function vibe ('map with a partial function based on your match, emit things that don't match ... very high expressivity'): xs.collect { case ... => ... }. Orchestrator's sketch: (1) clause lambdas, a lambda written as match arms; (2) an explicitly marked partial form that desugars to a match whose arms are wrapped in Some with a final _ => None, so it fits List.filterMap / a new List.collect (a → Option b); partiality is opt-in and visible, so the exhaustiveness check stays everywhere else. Questions for the note: syntax (fits lambda-syntax.md's grammar, the | ambiguity in one-line matches), how it reads in pipelines, Option vs a dedicated PartialFn with isDefinedAt, guards, other uses (Map.collect, Parse alternatives, orElse chaining), what proofs see (it is an ordinary match; collect membership lemma), and survey of AoC sites that would use it.
Progress (lane, 4 Nov 22:18): note written, docs/proposals/partial-lambdas.md (commit 3665220a1 on lane/SW-1292). Recommends design B: `match | …` clause lambdas (total), `match? | …` (arms wrapped in Some, rest None; for filterMap/findMap), `matches | …` (Boolean side, Scala's cond; rest False, body-less arm = True); guards `| p if c => e` as a later stage. Rejects C (partial by callee type) and D (PartialFn record). Decisions P1-P10 for Matt. Survey: 10 pipeline sites (5 need guards), 10 Option tables, 12 total clause lambdas, Boolean form 6 aoc + 13 std.

Merged as a proposal; awaiting Matt's decisions P1–P10 (asked as D2370: accept the recommendations?). Model result: Opus, worked, 11 min (+ the cond addition) (est. 60).

D2370 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): 'I really like this.' Spelling: match | … (total clause lambda), match some | … (Some for listed cases, None otherwise), matches | … (true for listed cases, false otherwise); replaces the note's match?. Other recommendations accepted; guards (P3) being discussed as D2371.

tickets.title: Pattern guards (| p if c => e) in every match; follows SW-1294
tickets.body:
D2371 (Matt, 4 Nov 2026): yes, as a follow-on stage after SW-1294. Stage 4 of docs/proposals/partial-lambdas.md (§6): | p if c => e in match … with, definition arms, and the three new forms (match, match some, matches). When the guard is false the arms below are tried; a guarded arm covers nothing for exhaustiveness (E-NONEXHAUSTIVE), so ordinary matches still need an unguarded arm, while match some / matches' hidden default covers the rest. Compiles to an if in the case tree whose else continues with the remaining arms; W-REDUNDANT with guarded arms; proofs see an ordinary if. Revives SW-237 (pruned without a note). Plan: Opus checks the design (a short note revising SW-237), then Sonnet implements; then migrate the five guarded pipeline sites (2024 days 6, 15, 20; 2021 day 18). Est. 3-4 h. Starts after SW-1294 merges.

Design note docs/proposals/pattern-guards.md (Opus, 15 min). Orchestrator's calls (minor, per Matt's overnight rule): (1) ship guards before generated equations exist (arms from the first guarded one get no equations/f.induct, E-NO-EQUATION with the reason); equations in a separate Opus lane; (2) migrate only 2024 day 15 positionsOf and 2021 day 18 orderedPairs (the others read better as filter/map); (3) guards may not perform operations (E-ABILITY), can be relaxed later. Implementation: Sonnet, same branch, est. 3-4 h.

Implemented (Sonnet, ~50 min, est. 210). Departure from the note: the kernel allows case only at the top of a body or branch, so the compiler makes the splits later rows need above the guard; the else tree holds only guards, leaves and missing cases. New E-GUARD-ARMS (absurd arm below a guard), E-MATCH-SIZE. AoC: 2024 d15 positionsOf, 2021 d18 orderedPairs. Opus review started 00:45 (generates kernel terms); day 18's audit went 15 -> 16 vacuity warnings, to explain. Findings: note §3.2 to correct; 'b != 0 && c != 0' gives no b ≠ 0 fact in an if (possible SW-226 gap).

Blocking: E-MALFORMED in the kernel when an arm below a guard is itself a match (in_tree not switched off for the else's leaves). Fix before merge: indexed-family matches falsely non-exhaustive after a guard; false E-GUARD-ARMS for nested (). Also: size limit too low for linear shapes; a misleading E-NO-EQUATION hint; note §3.2/§4 corrections. Sent back to the Sonnet lane (est. 60 min). Conjunction facts filed as SW-1305.

Review fixes done (7decb219e, d04608994): match bodies below a guard lifted; indexed missing cases tried with empty_case (and an impossible branch's guarded arms still type-checked); unit pattern below a guard; E-MATCH-SIZE 4096; hint and note corrections. tickets.title: if p && q (and auto generally) doesn't give each conjunct: 'if b != 0 && c != 0 then a % b' is E-AUTO-STUCK
tickets.body:
Found in the SW-1295 review, confirmed on main: neither an if on a conjunction nor auto splits p ∧ q into its parts, so 'if b != 0 && c != 0 then a % b else 0' fails with E-AUTO-STUCK (can't decide b ≠ 0); also with ∧, ≠ and b > 0 && c > 0. SW-226 only promised the right side of && knows the left. Applies to guards too ('| x if p && q =>'). Likely small in auto: split conjunction hypotheses.

DeepSeek attempt (branch ds/SW-1305, 18c225a1b; ~60 min) works on the examples but not merged: beyond its brief it changed how every 'if b && c' on propositions elaborates (both branches elaborated twice, the conjunction form kept only if a branch's auto proof uses it; doubling cost for nested ifs) and refactored unused_proof_if, which conflicts with SW-1295's check_if. Orchestrator's call: rerun on Opus, using the attempt as a reference. Model result: DeepSeek, failed (went past the brief's limit into a general change to if; design-level), 60 min (est. 60).

Opus lane (lane/SW-1305, f98bc2c74; started 02:01, done ~02:36, est. 90 min). The Bool reading of `a && b` records on the way the conjunction its operands decide (decided props, or a Bool c as c = True; at least one prop; b not using a's proof) with decision `Decidable.andThen da (_ => db)` (new std def, short-circuits like &&). `if` on it goes through the decided path like `if b != 0`; unused proof → the recorded Bool reading, so terms unchanged (prelude snapshot: only the two new defs added). One elaboration of the condition and branches. auto: parts of conjunction hypotheses (And.left/right, 8 deep) as a last step. Checks: elab lane, examples+hashes for auto-conjunction/pattern-guard, binary(hash_stability), std self-tests, aoc + rogue check: all pass. Bench: the check-number-*/text-literal/nested-parens "regressions" are identical on main without the change (stale baseline). Not covered: `if n != 0 && len % n == 0 then len / n` (b uses a's proof; needs a dependent conjunction), proof-valued ifs (check_proof_if keeps the Bool form).

Done on Opus (f98bc2c74, 35 min, est. 90): logic::condition records a ∧ b and a decision (new std Decidable.andThen/andYes) while reading a && b as Bool; check_if_in then takes the same path as 'if b != 0' (unused proof falls back to the original Bool term, so no hash moves; prelude snapshot gains the two new functions); auto tries conjunction parts last, depth 8. Guards benefit. Not covered: 'if n != 0 && len % n == 0' (dependent conjunction). Orchestrator's calls (minor): a Bool operand reads as c = True inside a conjunction, keep; the two std functions, yes. Bench drift is the stale 2 Nov baseline (identical with the change stashed).

Merged 2f7bf899b; verified: merge tier 1078/1078, hashes, fmt, natives, std_library, guide, aoc check and 1364 tests, rogue, audit. Model result: Opus, worked, 35 min (est. 90).

tickets.title: With SW-1227's guard off, 2021 day 2's aimedDepthCons fails on two terms that print identically: a gap comparing functions inside them?
tickets.body:
From SW-1227: the guard in one_step_apart avoids it, but the unifier failing on two identically printed terms suggests a comparison gap worth a look.

Done on lane/SW-1315 (8e6777f6b fix, 5a0a495fe moved hashes; on top of lane/SW-1227; Opus, 30 min, est. 90). Cause: force swaps in a solved unknown only at a value's head, so a call stuck on an unknown in its arguments stays stuck after that unknown is solved later in the same comparison; it prints with the solution, so the two sides look equal. Happens on main too (examples/accept/solved-after-stuck.sw: 'x + x = x + x' against itself). Fix: when a pair fails and a side is stuck on a since-solved unknown, read both back, evaluate again and compare once more. Orchestrator's calls: accept the four std/example hash moves (Text.fromListEq, stripPrefixTake, stripSuffixDrop, indexed-families append; migration cost never counts); keep SW-1227's guard for now. Merges after SW-1227 and SW-1314 with the same daily-tier run. Model result: Opus, worked, 30 min (est. 90).

Also fixes SW-1323 (an index 3 against 1 + 2 in an indexed family). Before merging, add its repro as an accept example.

tickets.title: A list literal [f x, ..rest] in a recursive result compiles to plain recursion, where Cons (f x) rest becomes a loop (tail recursion modulo cons); and it elaborates to a different term (hashes differ)
tickets.body:
Found by SW-1256's verifier: with List.map written [f x, ..List.map xs f], extract's more_tail_calls_are_loops overflowed the JS stack on 1,000,000 elements. List.map, takeWhile, spanOnto reverted to Cons on main. Find why a list literal with a spread doesn't elaborate to the same Cons term (SW-1221 noted the hash difference), make it do so, or make codegen see the loop; then convert those three back. Other converted sites (Parse, Reads, Terminal, aoc) may also have lost loops: check generated code for each.

Done on lane/SW-1324 (75e1e06d9; Sonnet, 41 min, est. 75). Cause: in a computation, a list literal went through comp_compound's infer, which wrapped the constructor in an annotation the JS loop detection didn't see; Cons went through comp_call as a constructor-as-lambda application. Fix (effects.rs): check Expr::List against the expected type; new comp_ctor_app builds a fully applied constructor from its fields' results. Now both forms are the same term; List.map, takeWhile, spanOnto back to brackets; 130 hash snapshots move (List.map's users). Changes elaboration of constructors in computations, so an independent Opus review started 06:45. Model result: Sonnet, worked, 41 min (est. 75). Finding: comp_app still uses the lambda form for named or partial constructor applications with a performing argument (low priority).

Review (Opus, 12 min): one blocking regression, fixed in de90f4a6f: a performing comparison in a constructor's Bool field (MkFlag (len() < 3)) wasn't decided; fields now go through run_argument with their slot types, as in comp_app. Order, once-only, implicit, dependent and proof fields, and the List check all held. Pre-existing gap filed as SW-1325.

Merged 9bfa4b6b5; verified: merge tier 1081, hashes, extract 60/60, std tests, aoc check and 1368 tests, rogue check and 100 tests, full audit.

tickets.title: Research and design note: non-empty lists in std (NonEmpty with reduce, head, last, maximum without Option), as Idris, Lean, Agda and Haskell do it; where the code base would model its data better with it
tickets.body:
D2383 (Matt, 5 Nov): 'let's file tickets to look at how we might do non-empty lists in the standard library so that we can have things like reduce, probably lots of other useful things. I'd be interested to see what our options are for this, what other languages like Idris, Lean, Agda [do]. What opportunities there might be in the existing code base to use it to better model the data. I think, in a way, having more precise types is powerful.' Options to compare: a record { head, tail }, a List with a proof (xs ≠ [] as a refinement / subtype), an indexed Vec (n+1), Haskell's NonEmpty; conversions, pattern syntax ([x, ..xs] for both?), how parsers (many1, sepBy1, lines, sections) would return it, how proofs use it. Survey std (maximum, minimum, last, head?) and aoc/rogue for Option-returning or partial uses that a non-empty type would remove. Opus.

tickets.title: Lanes adding an example keep missing its hash snapshot: SW-1359, SW-1379 and SW-1420 each reported snap:hashes NAME=examples passing with no .snap change, yet main's hash_stability examples failed on their new examples' missing snapshots. Find why the lane run passes (stale binary? INSTA settings? kache?) and make a missing snapshot fail it
tickets.body:
Found by batch 35's verifier, 5 Nov 2026. Each cost a verifier round.

Likely cause (SW-1429's lane, 5 Nov): snap:hashes NAME=examples is a name filter that matches no snapshot file, so it runs nothing and 'passes'. Lanes and my briefs say NAME=examples. Fix the task (make NAME=examples mean the examples sweep, or fail when the filter matches nothing) and the briefs.

Confirmed (Taskfile.yml:376): snap:hashes passes NAME to EXAMPLES, a filter on example file names; NAME=examples or NAME=prelude matches no file, so nothing new is snapshotted and it passes. The briefs were wrong (mine). Fix: hash_stability fails when EXAMPLES matches no file (name the filter), and the briefs say NAME=<the new example's file name> (or no NAME).

Done (3ca41cf65, 8151ba16e): hash_stability, cli examples and run_js fail when an EXAMPLES part names no example or project anywhere under examples/, with the nearest names; snap:hashes desc says NAME is an example file name. Second pass after review: one shared name set for every binary (a reject example or project name must not fail run_js). Merged. Model result: DeepSeek, needed fixes (per-binary name sets), ~25 + 15 min (est. 30).
